title: Clause-chain lab
subtitle: Keep main clause and dependent material distinct.
overview: A long Greek sentence becomes manageable when every dependent unit is attached to a finite-verb skeleton.
Use brackets for clauses and arrows for participles and prepositional phrases; only then form a connected translation.

items.grc: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὅτι ἐὰν πιστεύσητε ὄψεσθε τὴν δόξαν τοῦ θεοῦ.
items.en: He says to them that if you believe, you will see the glory of God.

items.grc: ὁ ἀκούων τὸν λόγον καὶ πιστεύων τῷ πέμψαντί με ἔχει ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
items.en: The one hearing the word and believing the one who sent me has eternal life.
